title: A royal mouth, an unprotected back
literal_meaning: The mouth is a king; the back is unprotected.
meaning_odia: ତୁଣ୍ଡରେ ରାଜାପରି ଦର୍ପ, କିନ୍ତୁ ପିଠି ଅରକ୍ଷିତ—ଏହି ବିରୋଧକୁ ଆମେ କଥାର ଦମ୍ଭ ଓ ତାହାର ପରିଣାମ ସାମ୍ନା କରିବାର ଅସହାୟତା ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ପାଠ-ଟୀକା: ମୂଳରେ ଥିବା ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ରକୁ ଅର୍ଥସଙ୍ଗତି ପାଇଁ ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର ବୋଲି ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି; ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଠରୁ ଏହି ସଂଶୋଧନ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: The mouth assumes royal authority while the back has no protection. Our editorial reading is that confident or domineering speech can exceed the speaker’s ability to face its consequences. Textual note: the uploaded ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର is conjecturally read as ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର, “king”; no second witness has confirmed that correction.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone makes sweeping demands on behalf of a group without checking whether anyone will support them. A colleague recalls the royal mouth and the unprotected back.
cultural_context: Two parts of one body carry opposite conditions: authority at the mouth and vulnerability at the back. The compact contrast gives speech a power that the rest of the speaker may not possess.

witnesses.note: Original: ତୁଣ୍ଡ ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର , ପିଠି ଅରକ୍ଷିତ। Display conjecturally changes ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର to ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର (king), a one-letter editorial correction without external confirmation; comma spacing regularised. ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର→ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନ; ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଠରୁ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।
